title: Reconfiguration of pseudocapacitive behavior and optimization of charge transport by Sr-doped CeFeO 3  perovskite nanoparticles
content: Ce1−xSrxFeO3 nanoparticles (x = 0, 0.35, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50, 0.55) were synthesized by co-precipitation to examine how A-site Sr2+ substitution affects their structural, morphological, vibrational, optical, dielectric, and electrochemical properties. XRD showed a single-phase cubic structure, validated by X-ray diffraction with a small, non-monotonic lattice expansion and a crystallite-size minimum of 21.17 nm at x = 0.45. FTIR identified the Fe–O stretching mode near 540 cm−1 and an additional band at 1114 cm−1 that appears only after Sr substitution. The optical band gap narrowed from 3.36 to 2.82 eV, while the Fe3+ d–d photoluminescence band stayed fixed near 745 nm and was progressively quenched at higher Sr content, consistent with vacancy-related non-radiative recombination. The dielectric response (1 kHz–2 MHz) peaked at x = 0.45 (ε′ ≈ 40), coinciding with the maximum dislocation density, and is attributed to Maxwell–Wagner interfacial polarization and Fe3+/Fe4+ hopping. Cyclic voltammetry indicated pseudocapacitive behavior, with a maximum specific capacitance of 328.4 F g−1 at x = 0.40 at 10 mV s−1 in 6 M KOH to 171.9 F g−1 at x = 0.45, while impedance decreased with increasing Sr content. The dielectric and electrochemical optima therefore fall at different compositions, indicating that grain-boundary space-charge polarization and faradaic charge storage are governed by different defect populations. These results identify x = 0.45 as the most favorable composition for dielectric response and x = 0.40 for charge storage in the Ce1−xSrxFeO3 system.
